questions.stem: The formula of the coordination compound which shows both coordination isomerism and linkage isomerism is:
questions.solution: Coordination isomerism requires both cationic and anionic complex species (present in A, C, D). Linkage isomerism requires an ambidentate ligand. In option C, $\mathrm{SCN^-}$ is an ambidentate ligand (can coordinate via S or N). Thus, C shows both types of isomerism.

questions.stem: The number of stereoisomers possible for the octahedral complex $[\text{Co}(\text{ox})_2(\text{Br})_2]^{3-}$ (where $\text{ox}$ is oxalate) is ________.
questions.solution:
The complex is of the type $[M(AA)_2B_2]$ where $AA$ is a symmetrical bidentate ligand.
This complex exhibits two geometrical isomers: cis and trans.
The trans-isomer is symmetrical (has plane of symmetry) and is optically inactive (1 form).
The cis-isomer is unsymmetrical (lacks plane of symmetry) and exists as a pair of enantiomers (dextro and laevo forms).
Total number of stereoisomers = 1 (trans) + 2 (cis-d & cis-l) = 3.

questions.stem: The complex showing optical activity is:
questions.solution: $\text{cis-}[\mathrm{Co(en)_2Cl_2}]^+$ lacks a plane of symmetry (and centre of symmetry) and is therefore chiral and optically active. Its trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive.

questions.stem: The total number of possible stereoisomers for the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is _______.
questions.solution:
$[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ exists as cis and trans isomers.
Trans-isomer is optically inactive (meso-like/symmetrical).
Cis-isomer exists as a pair of enantiomers ($d$ and $l$ form).
Total number of stereoisomers $= 1 \text{ (trans)} + 2 \text{ (cis- }d/l\text{)} = 3$.
